Theme

Work & responsibility

promote verb

raise to a higher rank or post

also promotion, get a promotion, be promoted, promoted, move up, move up a class, promote to the next grade

classical

Liv. 39.40.5: ad summōs honōrēs aliōs scientia jūris … prōvexit
Cic. Phil. 13.24: ecquō tē tua virtūs prōvexisset?

prōvehō, prōvehere, prōvexī, prōvectum

verb, third conjugation

advance, promote

To carry forward, and so to raise someone to a higher post (Lewis & Short). In the passive it is also to sail out, and to be carried away (longius prōvehī, to go too far).

Other words

  • 1prōmoveō: short o in the present stem (Lewis & Short prōmōveō). The simple verb is mŏveō in Lewis & Short; the long ō belongs to the perfect mōvī and the participle mōtus, and the compound keeps the short vowel of the present.

    prōmoveō1, prōmovēre, prōmōvī, prōmōtum — promote (to a post)

    verb, second conjugation · also used · classical · Plin. Ep. 7.31.3: prōmōtus ad amplissimās prōcūrātiōnēs (Lewis & Short); Traupman 187: ad (in) ampliōrem gradum prōmovēre, promote to a higher rank; Traupman 31: ad superiōrem classem prōmovēre, to promote (a pupil) to the next class

    In this sense post-Augustan (Curtius, Pliny, Suetonius); classically to move forward, push on (Caes. BC 2.11, Lewis & Short).

  • prōmōtiō, prōmōtiōnis f. — promotion (the noun)

    noun, third declension · also used · late Latin · Traupman 187; Lampr. Diadum. 2 (Lewis & Short)

    Late Latin (Lewis & Short); classical Latin uses the verb: prōvectus est, he was promoted.

Examples

  • ad summōs honōrēs aliōs scientia jūris, aliōs ēloquentia, aliōs glōria mīlitāris prōvexit

    some men were raised to the highest offices by their knowledge of law, some by their eloquence, some by their fame as soldiersLiv. 39.40.5

  • ecquō tē tua virtūs prōvexisset, ecquō genus vītae?

    how far would your own merit have got you, or your way of life?Cic. Phil. 13.24

  • ad (in) ampliōrem gradum prōmovēre

    to promote to a higher rankTraupman 365

  • ad superiōrem classem prōmovēre

    to promote (a pupil) to the next classTraupman 365

See also job, manager, employer, promote.

SourcesLewis & Short: proveho · Lewis & Short: promoveo · Lewis & Short: promotio
